## 3.3 Current Mole
At most one mole may be visible at any time. The current mole stores its type, selected hole, position, and remaining appearance time.
The hole is randomly selected from all 9 fixed holes. Two consecutive moles are allowed to appear at the same hole; the previous hole is not excluded from the next selection.
after: Each mole has its own independent appearance timer.
If a visible mole is clicked within its active duration, the corresponding score is awarded and that mole disappears immediately.
If a mole's appearance duration expires without a successful click, that mole disappears without changing the score.
The disappearance of one mole does not remove or reset the other active mole.
When both moles from the current pair have disappeared, a 0.3-second waiting period begins.
## 3.3 Active Moles
At most two moles may be visible at any time.
Each spawned pair contains exactly two moles. The two holes are randomly selected from the 9 fixed holes without replacement, so both moles must occupy different holes.
For each mole independently, the game stores:
- Type
- Selected hole
- Position
- Remaining appearance time
The mole types are selected independently, so a pair may contain:
- Two Normal Moles
- One Normal Mole and one Golden Mole
- Two Golden Moles
Each mole can award its score at most once.

before: The total game duration is fixed at 30 seconds. The countdown includes the initial waiting period, mole appearance periods, and waiting periods between moles.
after: The total game duration is fixed at 30 seconds. The countdown includes the initial waiting period, mole appearance periods, and waiting periods between mole pairs.

before: When the countdown reaches 0, the game immediately enters `game_over`. The current mole disappears, no new mole is spawned, no further click can change the score, and the display remains at `Time: 0`.
after: When the countdown reaches 0, the game immediately enters `game_over`. All active moles disappear, no new mole pair is spawned, no further click can change the score, and the display remains at `Time: 0`.

before: A mole is successfully clicked only when a left-mouse-button down event occurs within the current mole's 60 × 60 px clickable rectangle while that mole is active.
A successful click on a Normal Mole adds 1 point, while a successful click on a Golden Mole adds 3 points. The clicked mole then disappears immediately and a 0.3-second waiting period begins.
after: A mole is successfully clicked only when a left-mouse-button down event occurs within the 60 × 60 px clickable rectangle of one active mole while that mole is still active.
A successful click on a Normal Mole adds 1 point, while a successful click on a Golden Mole adds 3 points.
The clicked mole disappears immediately. If the other mole from the current pair remains active, it continues using its own existing appearance timer.
If the clicked mole was the final remaining mole from the current pair, a 0.3-second waiting period begins.

before: If a Normal Mole remains unclicked for 1.0 second, or a Golden Mole remains unclicked for 0.6 seconds, it disappears automatically. Missing a mole does not reduce the score or create any other penalty.
after: If a Normal Mole remains unclicked for 1.0 second, or a Golden Mole remains unclicked for 0.6 seconds, that mole disappears automatically.
Missing one mole does not reduce the score or affect the other mole's timer.
When the last active mole from the pair disappears, the next 0.3-second waiting period begins.

before: Restart resets the score, countdown, current mole, all mole-related timers, interface state, and game state. A new 0.3-second initial waiting period begins before the first mole appears.
after: Restart resets the score, countdown, all active moles, all mole-related timers, interface state, and game state. A new 0.3-second initial waiting period begins before the first mole pair appears.

before: Logical click detection always uses the current mole's 60 × 60 px rectangular clickable area, regardless of its visual shape.
A click succeeds if the mouse-down position lies within this rectangle while the mole is active. Pixel-perfect shape detection is not required.
after: Logical click detection always uses each active mole's 60 × 60 px rectangular clickable area, regardless of its visual shape.
A click succeeds if the mouse-down position lies within the rectangle of an active mole.
Because the two moles occupy different holes, their clickable rectangles do not overlap.
Pixel-perfect shape detection is not required.
